Print reference docs

Reads the reference docs one level at a time: with no topic it lists every topic; a topic lists its sections, each with the key to read it by (a topic with one section prints whole); a topic plus a section prints that section; `--full` prints the whole topic, as does `--dense`. With `--json`, a topic returns its whole doc, as docs() does, and `--index` its section index. A route opens a node of the docs tree: `cli` lists its guides and reference, `cli/api/functions` lists every API function, and `cli/api/functions/search` prints one. A namespace plus a section prints that section from the one guide below it that has it (`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs layout side-panels`). `--depth` reads as far down the tree as you ask, from the doc alone (0) to everything below it (all), and with it `--detail` sets how much of each doc below shows: one line (brief, the default), its sections (compact), or all of it (full).

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs [topic] [section]
```

Argument  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
--------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`topic`   | Doc topic to load (e.g. 'principles'), a docs-tree route (e.g. 'cli/api/functions/search'), or the name of one node of the docs tree: its own name (e.g. 'tokens-color'), or its route without the prefix its name repeats (e.g. 'tokens/color'), where exactly one node answers to it. Omit to list all topics.
`section` | Section to return: its key (from the topic's index), its title, or a unique part of its title (case-insensitive).                                                                                                                                                                                               

Option             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
------------------ | -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`--index`          | List the topic's sections and their keys, even for a topic with one section                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
`--full`           | Print the whole topic instead of its sections (text; `--json` returns the whole topic unless --index). Cannot be set with --index                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
`--depth <levels>` | How many levels of the docs tree to read below a namespace: 0 for the namespace alone, 1 for its children (what a read without --depth shows), all for everything below it. On the topic list, where a namespace otherwise lists alone, it names the docs below each one by the route that opens them, one line each. With it on a namespace read, --detail sets how much of each doc below shows: brief (one line each, the default), compact (with its sections), or full; the topic list is one line per doc whatever the detail

```bash
# List topics
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs
# A topic's sections
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs theme
# A whole topic as JSON
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs spacing --json
# One section
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs theme quick-start
# The CLI docs tree
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli
# Every CLI doc, one line each
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli --depth all
# Every route in the docs tree, one line each
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs --depth all
# The integration guides as one read
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring --depth all --detail full
# One API function
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/api/functions/search
# A whole guide
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/quick-start --full
```

Exit code | When                                                                                                                          
--------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0         | success                                                                                                                       
1         | unknown topic or route, a section that matches no section or more than one, or a --depth that is not a number of levels or all

Outside a project (`same`): it answers as it would in a new project on this release, reading this release's Core, as it does in a project with nothing installed: the one installed beside the CLI, else one in the per-user cache, which a global install downloads in the background after a command run online (in CI, the first command that needs it downloads it).

It runs `docs()` from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/api/functions/docs`.

astryx docs: Print reference docs. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/docs`.

Field | Type               | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
----- | ------------------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
name  | string             | yes      | Stable machine identity without the Astryx prefix, PascalCase. e.g. 'Button', 'TextInput', 'AppShell'. For an integration component it is the export apps import: the doc sits beside the file that exports it, and when that file exports nothing under its own name, `name` may name the export it does have. Change `displayName`, not `name`, to edit the visible label; registry URLs derive from this identity by default.
props | ComponentPropDoc[] | no       | SingleComponentDoc variant (required there): all public props for the one primary component. Each prop is {name, type, description, default?, required?, slotElements?, stability?}. Skip styling props like xstyle/className/style. Also present on SubComponentDoc.

ComponentDoc: The doc-type for a component directory's {Name}.doc.mjs. A discriminated union of SingleComponentDoc (props on the doc), MultiComponentDoc (a `components` array), and SubComponentDoc (a `subComponentOf` pointer). All three share the ComponentBaseDoc fields below; the variant is chosen by which of props / components / subComponentOf you set. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring component-doc`.
